contact.note: No published contact email was found in the checked official README, SECURITY.md, or SUPPORT.md. Example configuration values were not treated as project contacts.

article.summary: Browsentic is a local browser-agent harness with separate persistent context paths for a user profile, site-specific notes or generated maps, and recorded browsing workflows. This review examines selected source at a verified revision and does not run the application or measure memory quality or performance.

who_what.text: The official README presents Browsentic as a local browser harness that connects a browser extension and local Bridge to an agent CLI, with an optional MCP endpoint. This is an application with several browser-context stores, not a standalone hosted memory service; the README provides no email contact.

architecture.text: The profile is a validated JSON object containing contact fields, labeled details and standing instructions. The daemon reads and writes profile.json in local state; clearing all fields removes the file. Profile content is included in side-panel and scheduled-run prompts.

Site maps are directory-backed skill overlays. A generated map is represented by Markdown plus map.json, metadata, optional page notes, screenshots and robots/sitemap evidence. The report records summary, landmarks, pages, links and quirks; generated front matter carries domain, provenance and timestamp.

Recordings are held in the browser extension's local storage as an index and separate bodies. Bodies contain timestamped recorded events and may later include a normalized workflow; metadata records host, start URL, state, counts, duration and timestamps.

behavior.text: Profile updates replace the normalized profile document; clearing it deletes that file. Profile and standing-instruction prompt sections go to side-panel and scheduled tasks but not MCP clients, site mapping, file analysis or conversation titles.

Mapping is explicitly started, reads sitemap inputs and browses a bounded site, then validates and stages the generated result for review. Activation moves it into the uploaded skills directory; replacement stages the prior directory. A user can discard staged output or delete an active site map; the daemon sweeps abandoned staging after 24 hours.

Recording follows the user-started tab, caps a session at 15 minutes and filters sensitive fields by type, field name and card-like value. Analysis validates the generated steps. Stored recordings can be renamed or removed, and the oldest entry is dropped when the 20-recording cap is exceeded.

At prompt time, site overlays are selected by the active hostname and domain match; the longest match is prioritized, while an explicit @name can attach a note elsewhere. Authored overlays precede generated overlays. The prompt builder logs and omits notes that exceed a 64 KiB prompt; recording summaries have a separate 4 KiB budget and direct read tools can retrieve a chosen recording.

Profile data has local machine scope, site notes have domain metadata with optional explicit attachment, and recordings live in extension-local storage. These separate routing and storage rules do not establish a general multi-tenant or cross-principal isolation guarantee.

Site-map metadata records run ID, host, domain and generation time alongside captured sitemap evidence. Recorded events carry timestamps and URLs, but the inspected workflow model does not preserve a verified event-to-step evidence chain. Profile fields have no source citation or validity history.

Code-visible budgets include sitemap fetch limits of 20 documents, 4 MiB per document and 16 MiB total; mapping defaults of 15 pages, 10 screenshots and ten minutes; recordings of 2,000 events/15 minutes; and prompt limits of 64 KiB overall and 4 KiB for recording summaries. The code logs map lifecycle events and omitted prompt context. These are source observations, not measured performance.

metrics.evidence: Domain-selected notes, profile prompt content and recording lookup are implemented; no answerable or unanswerable probes were run.
Profile edits and site-map replacement are available; no fact-level correction or stale-value adjudication was run.
Profile clearing, map removal and recording removal are separate operations; no cross-store or post-deletion probes were run.
Host/domain selection and local storage boundaries are visible; no cross-principal or cross-browser isolation probes were run.
Site-map evidence files and recorded events exist, but generated memory claims were not adjudicated against them.
Prompt assembly and bounded retrieval-context paths are source-visible; no timing measurements were collected.
Prompt size limits are visible but no token usage or provider charges were measured.
Profile files, site-map directories and extension storage are visible; no bytes-per-item measurement was collected.

limits.text: This is a bounded inspection of selected source and documentation at one verified commit. Runtime behavior, map quality, recording fidelity, browser storage retention, authorization behavior and operational performance were not tested.
The profile, generated maps and recordings use separate persistence and deletion paths; deleting one category does not establish erasure from the others or across backups.

The official README and SECURITY.md were checked for a published email. The README directs general questions to contributing or GitHub discussions and SECURITY.md directs vulnerability reports through GitHub advisories; neither publishes a contact email, so contact_email is null.
